budget_items.what_was_said: A resident asked how the town band line item and concert sponsorships work; members gave conflicting figures for the line's size and agreed to follow up with the person who runs it.
The chair clarified, after initially misspeaking about Chapter 70, that Chapter 90 holds a balance over $2 million.
The chair said Chapter 70 aid has grown about 1.3% per year for the last four years, which everyone agrees needs addressing at the state level.
The chair said the town did not put money into stabilization this year and is effectively drawing down reserves for this one year, which is not best fiscal policy.
A member said last year's roughly one-million-dollar override went entirely to the school budget and remains there, compounding with the annual increase.
A member said that of 351 Massachusetts cities and towns, 16, including Lunenburg, passed an override designated for schools last year.

budget_items.topic: Town budget and tax rate sustainability
budget_items.what_was_said: A resident argued that a 2.5% annual increase and the current tax rate are unsustainable against a roughly $49 million town budget.
A resident explained cemetery fee mechanics, saying a cremation brings in a fee with nothing to perpetual care while a full burial is split between the burial-rights fund and perpetual care.
The same resident said the cemetery sale-of-lots account holds about $96,000 that is not visibly being used to improve the cemeteries.
The resident estimated roughly $6 per grave (or $4 a lot) to maintain about 6,000 graves, arguing current fees do not cover it.
The chair modeled scenarios showing excluded debt could reach about 12% against an 11% policy target if both the Marshall Park and municipal building debt exclusions pass.
The chair said the town was around 11% excluded debt in 2020 and was in excess of roughly 14% when the high school/middle school was built.
The chair modeled a hypothetical $110 million new Turkey Hill school with 50% MSBA reimbursement, netting about $55 million to the town, citing a $700 million Boston vocational school as context.
The chair said that over a 10-year period, excluding the override year, the town's tax levy actually grew about 4.2% per year on average, not just 2.5%.
The chair said the debt model assumed about 10% of the Marshall Park cost could be covered by grants.
A member said the reduced-scope Marshall Park proposal is priced at about $30 million and suggested asking the parks commission why that is the chosen scope.

budget_items.topic: School budget share of town budget
budget_items.what_was_said: A member said the school department is roughly 56% of the town's budget, making its lack of transparency a significant problem.
A member described watching a school committee meeting where a line-item transfer of roughly $16,000-$19,000 for copies was questioned but the underlying numbers were not spoken aloud.
A member reported the school athletic revolving account ran deficits of about $115,000 in 2024, $169,000 in 2023, and $120,000 this year, with the town covering the shortfall.
The same member said the athletic revolving account has run about $178,000 in the red cumulatively since 2020.
A member said the extended-day program does not fully cover its costs, with about $50,000 typically pulled from the school budget to cover it.
The chair said the town received about $880,000 last year, $690,000 the year before, and about $550,000 this year to cover school lunches, and funding would need to be found if that support ended.
A member said at least $120,000 of the roughly $948,000 override passed for the schools will go toward covering the FY25 athletic revolving account deficit.

budget_items.topic: School staffing cuts vs. budget increase
budget_items.what_was_said: A member described the confusing appearance of the school budget needing a 12% year-over-year increase while also cutting about 9% of staff and services.
A remote commenter called the town's $60,000 annual audit a poor use of money since it failed to catch known problems such as the parks revolving account.

minutes.headline: FinCom pressed the school committee on budget transparency and flagged growing revolving-fund deficits ahead of Town Meeting
minutes.summary: In its last meeting before Annual Town Meeting, the Finance Committee approved the consent calendar for town meeting, reviewed excluded-debt scenarios for the Marshall Park and municipal building projects, and heard extended public comment on free cash use, the school budget, and cemetery finances. Members spent much of the meeting criticizing the school department's budget transparency, citing unexplained line-item transfers and a growing athletic revolving-account deficit, and agreed to pursue records requests and a redesigned, earlier budget development timeline for next year.

what_happened.line: Finance Committee will file public records requests whenever school committee line-item transfers go unexplained, after criticizing school budget transparency and a growing athletic revolving-fund deficit.
The committee will work with the town manager, finance director, and incoming school business manager to redesign next year's budget development timeline.
Members reviewed excluded-debt scenarios showing the town's total could approach its own policy ceiling if both the Marshall Park and municipal building debt exclusions pass.
The committee voted to recommend approval of the consent calendar for Town Meeting, its last meeting before Town Meeting.
Public comment raised concerns about cemetery fund management and whether the town's tax rate is sustainable against the overall budget.

why_it_matters: A standing practice of records requests over unexplained school transfers could change what residents can see about how the school budget is actually managed before they vote on it.
If both proposed debt exclusions pass, the town's excluded debt would sit near a level it set for itself as a ceiling, a factor that shapes future tax bills.
Cemetery fee revenue and revolving-fund deficits (athletics, extended day) are services and fees residents pay into directly, and were flagged as not clearly tracking to their intended use.
watch_next: Annual Town Meeting vote on the consent calendar, the capital plan articles, and the debt exclusion questions
